Title: Shape Dart Cap
Content: Shape Dart Cap - Smooth Pattern outlines with darts. - Select the Edit Pattern tool from the 2D toolbar. - Hold down the Shift key on the keyboard and select two segments forming darts. - Right-click on the select segments and select Shape Dart Cap from the pop-up menu. - A black line appears showing how Pattern would look when darts are sewn. -Click and drag the red point on the black line to modify the curve as needed and hit the Enter key on the keyboard. - Pattern outlines with the dart are edited based on the modification. - Darts folded Pattern outlines appear as Baselines.

Title: Show Grading
Content: List of Contents Show Grading Show/hide Size Group Show/hide All Grading Show Grading - Show or hide grading from the 2D Patterns. - Show/hide Size Group Object Browser Grading Tab Size Group (Select Desired) Property Editor Show Show/hide All Grading 2D Toolbar Show Grading Main Menu Show 2D Pattern Show Grading Show/Hide Size Group - To show or hide specific Size Group, click the desired Size Group from the Object Browser Grading Tab. - Toggle off the Show option to hide the selected Size Group. - Toggle on to show the Size Group again. Show/Hide All Grading - To show or hide all grading, click the Show Grading tool from the 2D toolbar. - All grading in the 2D window disappears. - Click the Show Grading tool again to appear all grading.

Title: Shape Dart Cap
Content: Objective Smooth Pattern outlines with darts. Location Main Menu 2D Pattern Edit Edit Pattern 2D Toolbar Edit Pattern Operation Create a dart on a segment. Select the tool/menu indicated in Location. Right-click on the dart and select Shape Dart Cap. The Shape Dart Cap is displayed in light blue. Click a curve point Drag to smooth the connected line. Or, Click where there is no curve point to add and edit the curve point. (ver 7.3) Adjust curvature then press Enter. Shape Dart Cap is completed and the center line is created as the baseline. Note: If necessary, click the curve point to delete it with the Delete key. (ver 6.1)

Title: Edit V-Ray Light Properties
Content: Objective Configure the light properties for the final render image. Watch Tutorial Video Location Render Toolbar Light Properties Property Editor Operation Select the tool/menu indicated. The light properties appear in the Property Editor. Refer to the below table and edit the light properties as needed. It is recommended to use only necessary lights as the number of lights increase, the render speed may slow down. Option Description Preset (ver 7.1) Set the Preset for the light. When hovering the mouse over each presets, you can check the result of applying light in advance. Overall Intensity/Color Adjust the intensity and color of the light. Activate Activate or deactivate the light. Show Show or hide the light. Sphere, rectangle, and dome lights can be shown or hidden separately in the 3D/Render window. (ver 7.1) Dome Light Environment Map Load an Environment Map. Environment Map refers to light settings processed as an image (HDR). Light Angle Adjust the angle of the light shines on Avatars. Rectangle Light (Three-Point Light) Width/ Height Adjust the width and height of the Rectangle Lights. Note: * To create a three-dimensional render image, there must be a key light. Add key lights as needed to create more dynamic images. * When the Rectangle Lights are used along with the Dome Light, generally, a Rectangle Light is used as a key light. Thus, when using Rectangle Lights in combination with the Dome Light, use a HDRI image without a bright spot which acts as a key light. Sphere Light Radius Set the radius of the Sphere Light. Spot Light Cone Angle Adjust the angle of the Spot Light. The higher the value is, the wider the light area is. Penumbra Angle Adjust the penumbra angle. The higher the value is, the blended the light is. Shadow Radius Adjust the sharpness of the shadow. The higher the value is, the blended the shadow is. IES Light IES File Load an IES light file. An IES file stores the data of the brightness and shape of the actual light in real-life. Intensity (lm) Specified: The light intensity of the file is applied as-is. Custom: Adjust the light's intensity as needed. Ground Shadow Show or hide shadows on the ground. Note: Use theOpen,Savebuttons on the top of the Property Editor to save, open, and reuse the setting.

Title: Topstitch Item/Property
Content: List of Contents Topstitch Item Topstitch Item List Editing Topstitch Item Utilizing Topstitch Item Topstitch Item - Create and edit Topstitch items. - Navigate to Object Browser Topstitch Tab Topstitch Item List - Default_Topstitch is part of the program asset which is created upon download. It is fixed in the list and cannot be deleted. Adding Topstitch Item - Navigate to Object Browser Topstitch Tab Add Button - A new Topstitch item is created. Duplicating Topstitch Item - Click on the Topstitch item to be duplicated. - The Copy button above the Topstitch List is activated. - Click the Copy button as a duplicated Topstitch will be created at the bottom of the list. Deleting Topstitch Item - Only unused Topstitch item can be deleted. - Click on the Delete icon located at the right side of the Topstitch item. - Or right-click on the Topstitch item to access the pop-up menu. Select Delete. Editing Topstitch Item - Select the Topstitch item to be edited and navigate to Object Browser. Name - Change name for the selected Topstitch item. Type - There are two types of Topstitches: OBJ and Texture. -Select desired option. Material Preset - Select shapes of Topstitches among provided options: Custom, Bartack, Buttonhole, Overlock,Pickstitch, Single, Single_Offset_0, Zigzag. - When either Buttonhole or Overlock is selected, an additional option Stitch Width will appear. Color - Click on the color chip to change Topstitch color. - Click on the drop-down arrow next to Color to access child options: Ambient Intensity and Diffuse Intensity. - Adjust each option as needed. Offset - Commonly used offset values are provided as preset. - Input specified value as needed. - The unit corresponds to the unit that is currently used in CLO. Length (SPI) - Adjust the length of each Stitch. - SPI is the abbreviation for Stitch per Inch. As SPI increases, each Stitch length shortens. - Input specified stitch length as needed. Thread Thickness - Adjust the Thickness of the Thread manually. - Expand the drop down menus by clicking the Arrow button. - Choose the desired unit used for Thread Thickness among Tex, Ticket (Tkt,) Metric (Nm,) Denier (Den,) and Millimeter. - When Preset is set as Pickstitch, a child option is added to adjust distance in between each Stitch. Face - Choose the Topstitchs placement on the fabric: Front, Back, Both Number of Line - Assign number of lines for a Topstitch item. - When more than two lines are created, a child option Distance will appear. Use this option to adjust the apart distance of lines. - Select among provided values or input custom values as needed. Multilayered Topstitch - When a Topstitch item is created, only one layer is created by default. - To create multilayered Topstitch, click the + tab next to 1 tab. - Toggle On Use This Stitch option. The options will be activated. - Adjust options as needed. - As many as five layers of Stitches can be created to express complicated Stitch styles such as Color Overlock. Multilayered Topstitch_ver.4.1.0 and Above - Create various different types of Topstitches up to five at a time. - Choose the desired number of Topstitch lines using the drop down menu next to Stitch Count. - To configure multiple lines of a single Topstitch style at the same time, toggle on below options as needed. - Use Same Specification: Toggle on this option to configure multiple topstitches' Specification related options such as Shape, Length, Space and more at the same time. - Use Material: Toggle on this option to configure multiple topstitches' Material related options such as Texture, Color, Type and more at the same time. Default Topstitch Tread Thickness Unit_ver.4.2.0 and avobe - Change the default unit for Topstitch thickness. - Navigate to Main Menu Settings User Settings User Interface Default Topstitch Thread Thickness Unit - Select the desired unit among five options. Space_ver.4.2.0 and avobe - Set the distance between each stitch of Topstitch style. - The Space value can be both negative and positive values. Utilizing Topstitch Item Saving/Opening Topstitch Item - Select the Topstitch item to be saved. - Click on the Save button at the top of the properties. - A file browser will appear. Designate file name and path, and then click on the Save button. - The Topstitch item will be saved as .sst format. - To open a Topstitch item, select the Open button at the top of the properties. - When a file browser appears, located and open the Topstitch item to be opened. Applying Topstitch Item - Select the Edit Topstitch tool from the 2D toolbar. - Then, navigate to 2D window and select on the Topstitch line created on 2D Pattern. The selected Topstitch line will be highlighted in pink. - Click Assign button. - The selected Topstitch item will be applied to the Topstitch line created on 2D Pattern. - Or right-click on the Topstitch line on 2D Pattern to access a pop-up menu. - Select Assign to New Topstitch. - A new Topstitch item is created as it is automatically assigned to the selected Topstitch line on 2D Pattern. (Reference Editing Topstitch)

Title: Show UV Guide
Content: Show UV Guide - Check the UV area before exporting the 3D Garment. - Select the Show UV Guide tool from the 2D toolbar. - Or, navigate to and select Main Menu Display 2D Pattern Show UV Guide. - When the Show UV Guide tool is activated, the marquee box showing the UV area will appear.

Title: Edit Puckering
Content: List of Contents Edit Puckering Select Puckering Edit Length Move Puckering Puckering Right Click Pop-Up Menu Edit Puckering Properties Edit Puckering - Select and edit Puckerings in the 2D window. - Select the Edit Puckering tool from the 2D toolbar. - Or, navigate to and select Main Menu Materials Puckering Edit Puckering. Select Puckering - With the Edit Puckering tool selected, click on the Puckering on the 3D Garment. - The selected Puckering will be bolded. Edit Length - With the Edit Puckering tool selected, click and drag either end of the Puckering towards the direction it will be abridged or extended. Move Puckering - With the Edit Puckering tool selected, click and drag the Puckering. Release the mouse to complete. Puckering Right Click Pop-Up Menu - With the Edit Puckering tool, right click on the Puckering to access the pop-up menu. Select All with Same Property - Select all Puckerings that have the same property with the selected Puckering. Assign to New Puckering - A new Puckering item will be added to the Object Browser and the newly created Puckering item will be applied to the selected Puckering. Delete - Delete the selected Puckering. - Select the Puckering and hit the Delete key on the keyboard. Edit Puckering Properties - Modify each Puckerings properties individually. - Select the Edit Puckering tool. The selected Puckerings properties will appear in the Property Editor. Name - View and edit the name of the selected Puckering. Puckering Property - Select the Puckering item. - The Puckering list is the same with the list in the Object Browser. Extend Start/End - Extend the Puckerings to the Pattern outline. - Toggle on when Puckering is not adjacent to the Pattern outline. Puckering Placement (Only Applicable to Seamline Puckering). - Decide on which side of the seamline the Puckering will appear. - You can show the Puckering on either side or on both sides of the seamline.

Title: History Window
Content: List of Contents 3D State Delete &amp Rename Objective Keep track of your workflow with the History window and revert to previous points at any given time. In addition, save 3D states to review and compare specific points of progress. Location 3D State History Window 3D State Delete &amp Rename Right-click Pop-Up Menu (on 3D State) Delete or Rename Operation 3D State Follow the indicated guideline below: History Window 3D State Double click the desired 3D State. Warning as follows appears: "Loading the 3D State will delete the current History. Would you like to proceed?" Select OK. The 3D garment is reverted to the selected 3D State. Delete &amp Rename Follow the indicated guideline below: Right-click Pop-Up Menu (on 3D State) Delete or Rename The name field is highlighted and name can be changed. Title: Delete Buttonhole Style
Content: Objective Delete unnecessary buttonhole styles. Location Object Browser Buttonhole Tab Operation Follow the indicated guideline below: Object Browser Buttonhole Tab Select a buttonhole style to be deleted. Press the Delete key on keyboard or right click on the buttonhole style and select Delete. The selected buttonhole style is deleted.

Title: Puckering Properties and Options
Content: Objective Edit Puckering properties individually. Location 2D Window Toolbar Edit Puckering Operation Select a segment of applied puckering using the tool in the Location. Puckering properties appear in the Property Editor. Adjust the properties as needed. Property Description Name Rename the Puckering. Puckering Property Change the Puckering style applied to the selected segment. Extend Extend the start/endpoint of the puckering to the 2D pattern outline. Placement Select the desired placement by checking Both Sides. Offset Offset Adjust the distance between a puckering and a pattern outline. Include the Puckering Width in Offset or not if needed. Z-Offset Adjust the distance between Z-axis and a pattern piece. Or, Right-click on the puckering to apply the options as needed. Menu Description Select All with Same property Select the puckerings with the same properties as the selected puckering. Assign to New Puckering Add and apply a new puckering style. Delete Delete puckering. Remove Linked Editing (ver 7.3) Remove linked edtiting of the symmetric puckering.

Title: 3D File (Alembic) Import/Export
Content: List of Contents Import Alembic Export Alembic Objective Import/Export the object, cache, normal, and animation data contained within an Alembic file (ver2.4.0). Location Import Alembic Main Menu File Import Alembic Export Alembic Main Menu File Export Alembic (HDF5) / Alembic (OGAWA) Operation Import Alembic Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu File Import Alembic The Open File window appears. Select the desired file and click OK. The Import Alembic window appears. Select the settings as needed and click OK. The Alembic file is imported based on the setting. FPS Sets the frame rate of the cache data. Scale Input the scale directly or select from the available units. Garment Position Move Garment to Start Position Moves the Garment to the location of the first frame (ver2.5.0). Export Alembic Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu File Export Alembic (HDF5) / Alembic (OGAWA) The Open File window appears. Designate the file saving path and the file name. Then, click OK. The Export Alembic window appears. Select the settings as needed and click OK. The file is exported as an Alembic file based on the setting. Object Unweld Exports the Vertex (points of the mesh) of the parts of the pattern that are sewn together into one line into multiple objects. Thickness exports for quad meshes available beginning version 2.3.0. (ver2.3.0). Weld Combines the Vertex (points of the mesh) of the parts of the pattern that are sewn together into one line into one point. Weld Selected Pattern: Weld based on the sewing line that connects the selected patterns (ver2.3.0). Thin Ensures that the thickness will not be exported even if the rendering thickness value is increased beforehand. Thick Exports a pattern with its rendering thickness values in its increased state. Combined UV Coordinates: Exports all Garment Pattern texture data fit to UV Coordinates ranging from 0 to 1. Include Avatar Shape: Save the Avatar as part of the file. FPS Sets the frame rate of the cache data. Step Adds/Subtracts frames for the recorded Animation according to the entered value. Frame Relative Sample Sets the low and high values for frame relative sampling. Scale Adjusts the scale of the file being exported when a value is entered or the desired unit from Unit in file to import is selected.

Title: [2D Tool] Segment Sewing
Content: Objective Establish Sewing Lines on segments of Patterns or Internal Shapes/Lines. Location Main Menu Sewing Segment Sewing 2D Toolbar Segment Sewing Operation Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu Sewing Segment Sewing 2D Toolbar Segment Sewing Click once on the Pattern segment to establish the first half of the seam. With the mouse cursor, hover over the segment to be sewn to the first half of the seam. Drag the mouse to make the the Directional Notches parallel to each other. Then, click to establish the second half of the seam. Note When Directional Notches are crossed, the Sewing Lines in the 3D window are crossed as well. When Patterns are simulated at this state, either one of the Patterns is reversed and then sewn to the other Pattern. Use the shortcut to establish M:N Sewing Lines. For more detail, please reference M:N Segment Sewing.

Title: Menu
Content: The Main Menu is located on the topmost left of the CLO 3D Modelist, and a pop-up menu can be launched by right clicking in the 3D Garment Window and the 2D Pattern Window for fast access to each function. The 3D Environment Pop-up Menu, the Avatar Pop-up Menu, and the Garment Pop-up Menu can be launched from the 3D Avatar Window, and the Pattern Edit Pop-up Menu, the Pattern, Line/Point, Seam Line Pop-up Menu, etc. can be launched from the 2D Pattern Window. Main Menu Located on the topmost left of the CLO 3D Modelist, it shows the menus for each function. Note: Use the Help menu to navigate to our Help Center with program manuals, online lessons, FAQ, community and more with tremendous helpful resources (ver5.0.0.)

Title: Add Point/Split Line
Content: Objective Add points and split a segment into multiple segments. Just simply click or enter values to add points on segments. Location Main Menu 2D Pattern Edit Add Point/Split Line 2D Toolbar Add Point/Split Line Operation Select the tool/menu indicated. Move the mouse cursor over the segment. Smart Guide is displayed and the mouse cursor snaps at the intersection with the segment. (ver 7.0) Click the segment where the point is to be added. Point is added at the segment Or right click on a line. Split Line window appears Set the option Split into Two lines Adjust by entering the length of both lines which are divided by the right clicked point, or by entering the ratio. Split by Length Enter the number of segments the selected line should be divided into. You can change the direction in which a point is added to a start/opposite/center basis. Uniform split Enter the number of segments the line should be divided into. The line is equally divided accordingly. Note: Use the Edit pattern to tool Select multiple segments and right click When you select Split select, additional points can be added to multiple segments as they are detected as a single line.

Title: Cut / Cut & Sew
Content: Objective Cut 2D patterns based on the Internal Line and Baseline. Location Transform Pattern/ Edit Pattern Tool Main Menu 2D Pattern Edit Transform Pattern / Edit Pattern 2D Toolbar Transform Pattern / Edit Pattern Trace Tool Main Menu 2D Pattern Trace 2D Toolbar Trace Operation Select the tool/menu indicated in Location. Right-click on the Internal Line/Shape and click Cut or Cut &amp Sew. The pattern is cut or cut &amp sewn based on the selected Internal Line. Note: If the point of the Internal Line is less than 5mm from the outline of the pattern, the Internal Line is extended immediately and cut. (ver 6.0)

Title: Unfold Symmetric Editing (with Sewing)
Content: List of Contents Unfold Symmetric Editing (with Sewing) Remove Linked Editing Objective Edit a single pattern symmetrically based on its center line. Location Unfold Symmetric Editing (with Sewing) Right-Click Pop-Up Menu (on Line) Unfold Symmetric Editing with Sewing Remove Linked Editing Right-Click Pop-Up Menu (on Pattern) Remove Linked Editing Operation Unfold Symmetric Editing (with Sewing) Select a Pattern Outline with the Edit Pattern tool. Select the tool/menu indicated in Location. The pattern unfolds as a symmetric pattern based on the selected line. Remove Linked Editing Select a Pattern with the Transform Pattern tool. Select the tool/menu indicated in Location. The linked editing is removed. Note: Right-click on the unfolded pattern which is not symmetric and select Half Symmetric Editing (with Sewing), it can be edited as a symmetric pattern. (ver 6.1)

Title: Show 2D Topstitches
Content: Show 2D Topstitches - Show or hide Topstitches in the 2D window at your convenience. - Main Menu Display Materials Show 2D Topstitches. - 2D Toolbar Show 2D Topstitches. - Click the Show 2D Topstitches tool from the 2D toolbar to hide Topstitches from the 2D Patterns. - To show Topstitches again, click the Show 2D Topstitches tool again.

Title: Copy/Save Current V-Ray Render Image
Content: List of Contents Copy/Save Current Image Copy Current Image Save Current Image Show in Saved Folder Copy/Save Current Image - Simply copy or save the image appears in the preview window to quickly utilize rendered images. Copy Current Image - Select the Copy Current Image tool from the Render toolbar. Save Current Image - Select the Save Current Image tool from the Render toolbar. Copy Current Image - Select the Copy Current image tool to copy the current preview image shown in the Render window. - The image is copied to the clipboard and can be pasted into another program. Save Current Image - Select the Save Current Image tool to save the current preview image shown in the Render window. - The Save Image File window appears allowing you to locate the saving path. - Name the file and locate the saving path and click Save. - The image is saved. Show in Saved Folder - To see saved images, click the Show in Saved Folder tool from the Render toolbar. - The folder located in the saving path assigned in the Image/Video Properties appears, showing saved render outputs.

Title: Show/Hide Seam Allowance
Content: Objective Show or hide seam allowances from the 2D window. Seam allowances can be shown and hidden in the Print Layout Mode as well. Location For versions 5.0 and later: Main Menu Display 2D Pattern Show Seam Allowance 2D Window 2D Pattern Display Show Seam Allowance For versions 4.2 and earlier: Main Menu 2D Pattern Edit Transform Pattern 2D Toolbar Transform Pattern Operation Follow the indicated location above based on your software version: For versions 5.0 and later, follow the path to the option either through the main menu or the vertical toggle bar in the 2D window. The seam allowances can be hidden again using the same path. For versions 4.2 and earlier, right-click into the empty space of the 2D window: In the right-click menu, select Show Seam Allowance. Repeat this to hide seam allowances again. Note: All seam allowances remain shown when the Seam Allowance tool is activated.

Title: Show/Hide Avatar
Content: List of Contents Avatar Display Icons Show Avatar Show Arrangement Point Show Bounding Volumes Show Avatar Measurements Show Avatar Tape Show 3D Lines Avatar Display Icons - Show or hide icons related to Avatars. - Navigate to the 3D window and hover over the second icon in the Vertical View Toggle Menu. Show Avatar - Click the Show Avatar icon to show or hide avatars from the 3D window. Show Arrangement Point - Click the Show Arrangement Point icon to show or hide arrangement points on Avatar. Show Bounding Volumes - Click the Show Bounding Volumes icon to show or hide bounding volumes on Avatar. Show Avatar Measurements - Click the Show Avatar Measurements icon to show or hide measurements on Avatars. Show Avatar Tape - Click the Show Avatar Tape icon to show or hide Avatar Tapes on Avatars. Show 3D Lines - Click the Show 3D Lines icon to show or hide 3D lines drawn on Avatar.

Title: Select Mesh (Lasso)
Content: List of Conetens Select Mesh (Lasso) Select Multiple Areas Delete Selection Invert Selection Select a Segment Select a Pattern Select Mesh(Box) - Select and move 3D Garment mesh as needed. - Hold down the Select Mesh (Box) tool on the 3D toolbar to access the child menus. Then, select the Select Mesh (Box) tool from the 3D toolbar. - Or, navigate to the Main Menu and select 3D Garment Select Mesh (Lasso). Select Multiple Areas - Select the Select Mesh (Lasso) tool from the 3D toolbar. - Patterns in the 2D window and 3D window will appear in yellow-green Mesh structure. - Click and drag on the Pattern to freehand Lasso selection as desired to select desired area. - Hold down the Shift and Ctrl keys on the keyboard to select multiple areas on the 3D Garment. Delete Selection - To deselect particular areas, hold down the Ctrl key on the keyboard and click and drag to encompass the desired area in the 2D window. The encompassed area will be deselected. Invert Selection - To invert the selection, hold down the Shift key on the keyboard to click and drag on the 3D Garment. - The areas originally not selected will be selected and vice-versa. - The selected area will be highlighted in yellow-green. Select a Segment - Double click on the Pattern outline in the 2D or 3D window to select a segment. Select a Pattern - Double click within the Pattern in the 2D or 3D window to select a Pattern.

Title: Fit Map
Content: List of Contents Fit Map Can't Wear vs. Tight Fit Map - Check the tightness of 3D Garments with the color scale. - Hover over the third icon in the Vertical View Toggle Menu in the 3D window and select the Fit Map icon. Can't Wear vs. Tight - When the Fit Map icon is selected, the 3D Garment will appear in white, yellow, and red, each indicating the tightness of the 3D Garment. - Red shows the Cant Wear areas on the 3D Garment, where the Garment is too tight, not possible to wear in real life. - The percentage of the Cant Wear areas will show on the Cant Wear boxs right. - Yellow shows the Tight areas on the 3D Garment, where the Garment is tight. - The percentage of the Tight areas will show on the Tight boxs right.

Title: Edit UV
Content: Edit UV - Change the Pattern placement and edit the UV layout in the 2D Window. - Select the Edit UV tool from the 2D toolbar. - Or, navigate to and select Main Menu Material Edit UV. Automatic - The Automatic option is set as default. - When the Edit UV tools setting is set as Automatic, the UV area will be automatically assigned, surrounding all Patterns in the 2D window. Manual - The marquee box surrounding all Patterns in the 2D window will appear when the Edit UV tool is activated. - Click the icon on the right top of the marquee box. - The Edit UV tools setting will be changed to Manual, allowing users to manually edit the UV area. - When the marquee box changes to light blue, click and drag the marquee box to resize the UV area. - Select and move the Patterns to rearrange them within the UV area.

Title: Delete Arrangement Point
Content: Objective Delete Arrangement Points no longer in need. Location Main Menu Avatar Avatar Editor Arrangement Arrangement Point Delete Operation Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu Avatar Avatar Editor Arrangement Arrangement Point Delete Selected Arrangement Point is now being deleted from the Arrangement Point list and the 3D window.

Title: Buttonhole List Window
Content: It is possible to create, copy, apply and set a style in Buttonhole list window. Without any extra setting, the Default Buttonhole is applied as default. Once the Default Buttonhole style is modified, it lasts until rerun of the program and it is unable to be deleted.

Title: HASP driver settings for CLO offline-auth products
Content: The Latest HASP driver download (updated June 2022) Mac: https://cdn.clo3d.com/HASP/Sentinel_Runtime_94691.tar Linux: https://cdn.clo3d.com/HASP/aksusbd-8.31.1.tar Windows: https://cdn.clo3d.com/HASP/haspdinst_8_31.exe Sentinel HASP Driver Errors on Windows Objective The Sentinel HASP Diver is automatically installed with the software, but it fails occasionally. Please download and install the Sentinel HASP Driver which is suitable for your operating system. Operation Installing Sentinel Driver on Windows Download the latest HASP driver (See above) Enter "CMD" in 'Windows Start Button + Run (R)' to install the driver. Drag the downloaded haspdinst.exe file and put it on the CMD window to automatically register the corresponding path as shown underlined below. Enter "-i" behind the automatically entered path and press 'Enter' on keyboard to install. Access to http://localhost:1947 and check to see if the following screen appears to see if the HASP Driver has been successfully installed. If the following screen appears, then installation is successful. If the following error occurs, the HASP Driver must be deleted and reinstalled. HASP Driver Deletion Deleting Sentinel Driver on Windows Download the latest HASP driver (see above) Enter "CMD" in 'Windows Start Button + Run (R)' to delete the driver. Drag the downloaded haspdinst.exe file and put it on the CMD window to automatically register the corresponding path as shown underlined below. Enter "-purge -r" behind the corresponding path and press 'Enter' on keyboard to delete. After the driver has been successfully deleted, refer to the following content to reinstall the driver. HASP Driver Installation Sentinel HASP Driver Errors on MAC Objective The Sentinel HASP Diver is automatically installed with the software, but it fails occasionally. Please download and install the Mac OS Sentinel HASP Driver. Operation Installing Sentinel Driver on Mac * Download the latest HASP driver (see above) * ver 21.0 Build 77815 Sentinel Driver for Mac Supported Platforms: Mac OS X 10.9.x, 10.10.x, 10.11.x, 10.12.x, 10.13.x https://s3.clo3d.com/sentinel/7.80/Sentinel_Runtime.dmg * macOS Catalina 10.15 users, please download Sentinel Driver here https://s3.clo3d.com/sentinel/Sentinel_Runtime.dmg Please remove all the dongle keys inserted into the Mac PC installation to be done. Mount "Sentinel_Runtime.dmg" (ver 21.0 Build 77815) Double-click the Install Sentinel Runtime Environment icon. Please allow the 'hasplmd' application to accept incoming network connections (this message may not appear). Access to http://localhost:1947 If you are unable to connect to the URL, try again after 10 seconds later. If it still does not work, reboot and connect again. If the solutions above do not work, please go back to the first step and check again. *If you click Diagnostics, License Manager Version appears with newly installed version ver 21.0 Build 77815 (Version information of 21.0 Build 77815 appears as this in Diagnostics). Insert Dongle key into USB port. If the Dongle key appears in 'Sentinel Keys', the installation is successfully done. Reinstalling Sentinel on Mac Please remove all the dongle keys from USB port. Mount "Sentinel_Runtime.dmg" with version of "ver 21.0 Build 77815". Double-click Uninstall Sentinel Runtime Environment. Click Uninstall. If the un-installation is done normally, the dialog above appears. Please press OK button and then click Quit. Reboot your Mac. Install Sentinel Driver. Please refer to the following method Reinstall Sentinel Driver on Mac *If you don't follow the guideline, you may not be able to find Dongle keys inserted into your PC or other PCs. Also the other PCs may not be able to find your Dongle key. Sentinel Driver Known Bugs * Sentinel LDK Protection System Error : invalid XML scope (36) Normally occurred when operating in CLO3D modelist network dongle 1.4.14.7701 (Enveloped with Sentinel LDK 6.4 version or before 6.4). * Occurs with the following conditions: Network Dongle key (not a local Dongle key) CLO3D Modelist Network with 2.1.44 or later version. (Enveloped with Sentinel LDK 7.1) The Dongle key is inserted into another PC. The version of Sentinel Driver is 13.20 in your Mac. Operates normally after reinstalling with Mac Sentinel Driver ver 16.0. * If multiple Sentinel Drivers are mounted, the software is unable to find virtual files. Title: Video Capture (Preview and Edit)
Content: Objective Play preview and edit video. Location Turntable Video Capture Preview (Preview window that appears after the recording) Operation Preview Follow the indicated guideline below: Turntable Video Capture Preview (Preview window that appears after the recording) Utilize below buttons as needed. Note: Preview Option Start Moves to beginning of the play area. Play Plays the play area. Pause Pauses temporarily on the play area. End Moves to end of the play area. Repeat Repeats the play area. Edit Follow the indicated guideline below: Turntable Video Capture Preview (Preview window that appears after the recording) Click where to edit on the timeline. Frame bar appears. Right click on the frame bar, click 'Split'. The split play area is now being separated from the timeline. Unnecessary part is deletable by right-clicking and pressing 'Delete'.
